title: Global sections on a power-series open with punctured zero section
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian commutative local ring of depth at least two [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-depth], and let $d>0$ be an integer. Put $B=A[[X_1,\ldots,X_d]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], and let $z:\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ be the morphism induced by constant coefficient [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $V\subset\operatorname{Spec}B$ be open and suppose $z^{-1}(V)=\operatorname{Spec}A\setminus\{\mathfrak m_A\}$. The canonical ring homomorphism $B=\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}B,\mathcal O)\to\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$ is bijective. No reducedness, integrality, normality or nonempty-cover assumption is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0EY9, pione.tex, lemma-fully-faithful-power-series-over-depth2: first displayed comparison of global section rings in the proof; its injectivity detail is expanded using Tags 00IQ and 0311.

proof.text: Depth-two Hartogs on the punctured spectrum U of A gives Gamma(U,O)=A. Let I be the variable ideal in B=A[[X_1,...,X_d]]. Each B/I^n is finite free over A, on monomials of degree less than n. The induced thickenings of U in V therefore have section rings B/I^n, compatibly with reduction. Their inverse limit is B, since a compatible system of truncations determines every coefficient.

The constants inclusion A -> B is flat. The associated-prime base-change formula, applied to M=A and N=B, says that associated primes of B are exactly pB with p associated to A: B/pB is (A/p)[[X_1,...,X_d]], a domain. The bound depth(A) <= dim(A/p) excludes p=m_A. Thus pB specializes to pB+I, a zero-section point lying in U and hence in V. A section with zero formal restriction has germ in every power of I at each point of U. Krull intersection in that Noetherian local ring makes the germ zero. It is then zero at pB as well. On an affine neighbourhood of each point of V, the associated-prime localization criterion for its section module implies the section is zero: all its associated germs have just been shown to vanish. Consequently Gamma(V,O) -> lim Gamma(V_n,O) is injective.

The composite B -> Gamma(V,O) -> lim Gamma(V_n,O)=B is the identity, since it reduces to the usual quotient map at every n. Write r for the first map and c for the second. The identity c(r(b))=b makes r injective. For a section e, injectivity of c and c(r(c(e)))=c(e) give r(c(e))=e, so r is surjective. Under Gamma(Spec B,O)=B this r is the stated canonical map.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0EY9, first comparison; the omitted injectivity detail is expanded as in the parent node using associated primes and Krull intersection, with the associated-prime formula made explicit.

theorem bijective_powerSeries_punctured_globalSections
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (hdepth : (2 : ℕ∞) ≤ IsLocalRing.depth (R := A) A)
    (d : ℕ) (hd : 0 < d)
    (V : (Spec (.of (MvPowerSeries (Fin d) A))).Opens)
    (hV : ∀ x : Spec (.of A),
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (MvPowerSeries.constantCoeff (σ := Fin d)))) x ∈ V ↔
        x ≠ IsLocalRing.closedPoint A) :
    Function.Bijective
      ((ΓSpecIso (.of (MvPowerSeries (Fin d) A))).inv ≫ V.ι.appTop).hom
